validity.researcher_notes: Fetched the gem.wiki page directly (lead only, not cited) — it has two 'Project details' subsections, 'Badr El Din Spur (1)' (Capacity 180 MMcf/d, Length 130 km, Diameter 20 in) and 'Badr El Din Spur (2)' (Capacity 150 MMcf/d, Length 130 km, Diameter 16 in), both sourced to the same single footnote [1], which is the egyptoil-gas.com 'Western Desert' PDF (already the sheet's FuelSource URL). Downloaded that PDF independently and ran pdftotext -layout on it: it contains a 'Natural Gas Infrastructure in the Western Desert' table listing 13 named pipelines with From/To/Length/Diameter/Capacity columns, including two rows — 'Badr El Din Spur (1)': Badr El Din Fields -> BED/Abu Sennan connector, 130 km, 20 in, 180 mmcf/d; and 'Badr El Din Spur (2)': Badr El Din Fields -> BED/Abu Sennan connector, 130 km, 16 in, 150 mmcf/d. This exactly matches the sheet's current values for P3938 (Length 130 km, Diameter 16.00 in, Capacity 150 MMcf/d) and confirms segment (2) is correctly 16 in only — the wiki flag's '16 in; 20 in' union reflects both segments on the shared page, not a discrepancy on this row. No independent second source found with segment-level diameters for this specific spur pair (searched English and Arabic); treating the Egypt Oil & Gas trade-press table as the single strong (non-GEM) source.

validity.recommendation: UNRESOLVED — could not find a verifiable StartYear1 for this segment; do not guess/fill. Status=operating with no start year is a genuine sourcing gap, not necessarily an error: this is an old (likely 1980s-90s) internal Western Desert gas-gathering spur built by General Petroleum Company (GPC) alongside its Abu Sennan gas/condensate plant, and no public record with an exact commissioning year for the spur itself was located.
validity.researcher_notes: Checked the same egyptoil-gas.com Western Desert PDF (2020) — its 13-pipeline infrastructure table has no start-year/commissioning-date column at all, only From/To/Length/Diameter/Capacity. Ran multiple English-language web searches for 'Badr El Din Spur' + GPC/Abu Sennan + startup/commissioned/inaugurated/history/1990s, and Arabic-language searches for the pipeline and for GPC's Abu Sennan gas plant history (أنبوب الغاز بدر الدين أبو سنان). Found only: GPC itself was established 1957 (not usable as a pipeline start year); Shell's Badr El Din concession/BAPETCO JV dates to the 1980s and the Badr field gas/oil discovery is dated 1986 in some secondary sources; a Future Pipe Industries press release (2022) describes GPC building a newer, unrelated 24 km GRE gas pipeline phase in the Abu Senan area (different project, wrong length/material, not this spur). None of these sources gives a specific commissioning year for the Badr El Din Spur (1)/(2) pair itself. No fill staged — no ref exists to pair with a value, and rule 2/3 (no fabricated URL, never guess a date) apply directly.

summary: P3938 (Badr El Din Spur (2)): Diameter flag resolved — sheet's 16 in is correct (wiki union reflects both co-located segments, not this row); StartYear1 flag UNRESOLVED — no verifiable commissioning year found in English or Arabic sources, no fill staged.
